actual_scope: Prove, for any native P104 word obeying the frame law of the native verifier (public registers strictly ascend and are nested; owned registers may move in any direction; ADD/COPY/SCALE only at a common frame; COPY only into a zero owned register; no owned register left at exit; CLEAR may be dirty; helpers and singular endpoint maps allowed), that for every nonzero vector set Q the number of owned MOVE events from a frame meeting Q to a frame missing Q is at least rank T[final publics whose final frame misses Q, initial publics whose initial frame meets Q]. For a port clique W (q.q'=1 for all ports in W, including q=q') and W <= Q <= A(W) this rank is |W|, so a legal native has at least |W| such owned exits. Apply it to the native word of #6833 (9|9 chain-nested root): the bound is tight on all 1967 maximal port cliques, and every one-unit end shortening of each owned lifetime in two stated families (246 core replacement frames, 547 ascending-start variants) is infeasible, each with a stored (W,Q) certificate.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a joint helper basis and a legal causal split on the complete invoice. This package is a structural obstruction on the owned layer of one native word: it constructs no word, prices nothing, and says which one-unit changes of owned lifetime ends cannot be legal.
bottleneck_link: docs/research/research-family-status.md; the statement fixes a necessary condition on the owned-move events of any legal native and which end-shortening edits of the #6833 owned layer it excludes.
stop_rule: No kappa claim. The theorem is a necessary condition in the abstract legal model (frame law as stated, linear coefficients). It counts owned MOVE events, not dimension mass, and says nothing about edits that change several lifetimes at once, add moves, change the root, or relax the public-ascent rule (the public-descent control violates it). A certificate shows only that the stated owned-move multiset is infeasible; a survivor of the cut test would not be a feasibility claim. No word is constructed and nothing is priced.
evidence: README.md (statement and self-contained proof), check.py (exact replay of the #6833 native word against the frame law; 1967/1967 cliques tight; 246/246 core and 547/547 ascending-start variants certified; 31,000 exact random legal words with 0 violations; public-descent control with 65,551 violations).

open_questions.question: Do the owned-exit lower bounds from different cuts combine into a bound above 8 owned MOVE events, or into a dimension-mass bound, for a native word?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The cut bound counts events: one exit carries one vector whatever its dimension change. The word of #6833 is tight at 8 on every maximal clique, so single cuts cannot exclude removing mass while keeping 8 or more moves.
open_questions.first_step: Compute, for the 1967 maximal cliques, the exits of the word under every Q between W and A(W) and test whether a weighted family of cuts forces more than 8 events (an exact linear program over cut multiplicities).
open_questions.blocked_by: A mass statement needs an argument that charges dimension change to cut crossings; the present proof only charges one unit per event.

open_questions.question: Which multi-lifetime edits (moving or splitting hops of several owned lifetimes at once, or adding a move) survive every cut (W,Q)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The certificates cover one lifetime end shortened by one unit with all other lifetimes unchanged; the theorem applies to any edit by recomputing exits.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate two-lifetime edits that keep every clique's exit count at or above |W| and then test each survivor against the remaining native constraints.
open_questions.blocked_by: A survivor of the cut test is only a necessary-condition survivor; its feasibility needs a separate construction.

open_questions.question: Is there a companion bound for entries (owned ascents into U_Q) valid without an invertible endpoint map?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Owned ascent never exits an up-set, so the exit bound does not constrain ascending starts beyond deleting the replaced hop; an entry bound would constrain them directly.
open_questions.first_step: State the rank of the inverse endpoint block against entry events and test it with the same exact random-word replay for singular endpoint maps.
open_questions.blocked_by: The inverse form needs an invertible endpoint map; for the P104 forward native its relevant block is zero, so it gives no constraint there.
